comments.content: Issue 1 confirmed: FILE_CLAIM_RE uses `[a-z]{1,4}` to bound the file extension, which truncates longer extensions like .typescript, .javascript, .config, .module. The truncated path is then checked with `git cat-file -e`, producing false PHANTOM-DIFF hits on legitimate commits. Sibling scanners (scan-silent.sh, scan-stub.sh) were reviewed and do NOT parse claimed file extensions at all — they scan staged .ts source files with line-oriented regex, so there is no shared extension-length convention to align with. This makes the `[1,4]` bound an arbitrary constraint unique to this scanner. Recommendation: relax to `[a-z]{1,6}` or drop the extension-length bound entirely (`[^ ]+\.[a-z]+`) since the `git cat-file -e` lookup already validates file existence regardless of extension length.

Issue 2 is NOT confirmed as a real merge-commit blind spot. CLAIM_RE requires the subject to start with a semantic prefix (`^[a-z]+(\([^)]*\))?:[[:space:]]`), so merge commits with default subjects like `Merge branch 'x'` or `Merge pull request #N` do NOT match the completion-claim pattern and are naturally excluded from CHECK 1. No sibling scanner in `.githooks/` filters merges via `rev-list --merges/--no-merges` (verified via search), so there is no existing project convention to follow. The existing `^[a-z]+...` anchor already acts as an effective merge-exclusion. No fix required — this is a false positive in the review report.

Issue 3 confirmed: FILE_CLAIM_RE uses `[^ ]+` for the file path, which cannot match file paths containing spaces. A body claiming 'created my file.ts' would fail to match the regex at all, so the scan silently misses the claim even if the file truly does not exist — defeating CHECK 2's purpose. Sibling scanners (scan-silent.sh, scan-stub.sh) face a similar limitation: they are line-oriented and word-split on spaces, consistent with the project's existing tokenization convention. However, since file-claim detection is correctness-critical for this gate (a missed claim = a phantom that slips through), this is worth noting. No sibling scanner handles quoted/spaced paths, so there is no project convention to adopt. Recommendation: at minimum document this constraint, or use a more permissive trailing-token extractor.

comments.content: The scan_silent and scan_stub functions receive the working-tree filename ($f) and scan the ENTIRE file content, not the staged git diff. Both library functions read the file directly via `while IFS= read -r line` and `grep -nE ... "$f"` with no `git diff --cached` extraction. The gate headers on lines 81 and 91 explicitly state "PREDICATE READS: a staged src/**/*.ts diff" — but the implementation checks all lines, including unchanged pre-existing code. A developer who stages only part of a file (e.g. git add -p) or commits a file that already contains a silent-fallback/stub pattern they never touched will get a false rejection. This creates gate fatigue and --no-verify bypass. The fix: have the pre-commit hook pass the staged diff (via `git diff --cached -- "$f"`) to the scan functions, or have the scan functions extract added/modified lines internally rather than reading the whole file.

The inner while-loop then feeds every non-empty line to gate_reject as if it were a finding. While the scan functions currently only write structured output to stdout, any stray stderr from internal sed/tr/wc/grep diagnostics would be misreported as a W-13 or W-14 rejection, producing confusing messages. Since the functions are designed to emit findings on stdout exclusively, the capture should redirect stderr to a separate stream (or /dev/null) so only stdout lines are treated as findings. For example: `SILENT_OUT="$(scan_silent "$f" 2>/dev/null || true)"` — this preserves the `|| true` safety net while preventing stderr noise from being interpreted as findings.

New refs are never properly checked. On a first push of a new branch, there is no remote-tracking ref yet, so line 77 returns empty and the code falls to `git show --name-only` (line 85), which inspects only ONE commit instead of the full pushed range. Additionally, `break` (line 68) means only the first non-delete ref in a multi-ref push is captured.
